Usage

When to use. A tooltip is a read-only label that supplements an already-affordable control — clarify an icon-only button, surface the full text of a truncated string, or hint at a keyboard shortcut. Keep it short (a few words to one sentence) and non-critical: people on touch devices and keyboard-only users may never see it.

Do

  • Attach it to a focusable trigger and associate it with aria-describedby.
  • Default to the Above placement; flip sides only to avoid clipping.
  • Keep copy to a short phrase or a single sentence.
  • Wire up Escape to dismiss while leaving focus on the trigger (WCAG 1.4.13).

Don't

  • Put required information inside a tooltip — use a visible label or inline message.
  • Place links, buttons, or any focusable content in it — reach for a popover.
  • Use it for errors, confirmations, or anything that prompts a decision — use a callout or dialog.
  • Attach it to a non-interactive element that keyboard users can't reach.

Accessibility

  • Escape to dismiss. Always wire up an Escape handler that hides the tooltip while leaving focus on the trigger.
  • Associate the tooltip with its trigger. Set aria-describedby on the trigger pointing at the tooltip's id, or screen reader users receive no content.
  • Honor reduced motion. When prefers-reduced-motion: reduce is set, show and hide instantly — no fade.
